messages:
sara: FYI bringing up a new 3B from VendorX — 'Archer-3B'. License attached, looks a bit restrictive on redistribution. Can legal confirm hosted / quantization constraints? :wave:

matt: Can you paste the license text or a link? quick scan helps. :eyes:

sara: pasted below (excerpt):
```
Redistribution of Model Files (weights, converted binaries) is prohibited.
Derivative works for internal use permitted; commercial use requires separate agreement.
Attribution required: include "Archer-3B (VendorX)" in product docs.
```
Link: https://vendorx.com/licenses/archer-3b

matt: OK — red flags:
- 'Redistribution prohibited' means we cannot ship quantized weights or docker images to customers.
- 'Derivative for internal use' allows us to quantize and run internally (hosted or dedicated), but not distribute binaries.
- Attribution clause is straightforward but needs wording in our model card.

jess: Does 'commercial use requires separate agreement' block using Archer as a hosted inference model for paying customers? Thinking yes unless vendor signs a commercial license.

matt: Correct. Hosted API (public paid) = commercial. Dedicated/Private depends: if we run in our infra and only expose a service (no downloading weights), that's still commercial use but often acceptable under internal derivative clause — but the vendor language is vague. We should ask vendor for confirmation or an addendum.

oli: For Dedicated: we sometimes ship quantized images to customers (on-prem installers). That would be redistribution and therefore blocked. For Dedicated cloud instances (we control infra), we might be ok to host.

sara: For evals/benchmarks we planned to run quantize-and-bench on our infra and share perf numbers internally and in blog. Is public benchmarking allowed?

matt: Benchmarking results are usually fine if you don't publish the weights. Attribution still required when you mention model name. Don't include any downloadable artifacts.

sara: So immediate plan: run quant experiments on our infra, add a big-model gating note: 'VendorX requires commercial license to distribute binaries; hosting-only until license secured' — can we add to onboarding checklist?

matt: Yes — add a blocking item: 'license confirmed for commercial hosting/distribution' + vendor contact. Also ask vendor about a redistribution clause for quantized binaries (some vendors grant redistribution of quantized weights under separate fee).

sara: @legal-bot please create a ticket to track vendor conversation and license clearance

legal-bot: Ticket created: LEG-2026-1187 — vendorX Archer-3B commercial/redistribution query. Assigned to matt. :white_check_mark:

sara: thanks — will pause any customer-facing shipping and update the model card with the attribution + hosted-only note. :thumbsup:
